method: The WHO Global Physical Activity Questionnaire analysis guide assigns 8 METs to vigorous work and vigorous leisure activity and 4 METs to moderate work, moderate leisure and travel on foot or by bicycle. Each domain contributes days x minutes per active day x its MET value, and the five contributions sum to total MET-minutes per week. Days are whole numbers from 0 to 7 and minutes are whole numbers from 0 to 1440; a domain with days but no minutes, minutes without days, or an active day shorter than the 10-minute bout GPAQ counts is refused with the field named. Dividing the total by 4 gives moderate-equivalent minutes, and the total is compared with the WHO recommendation of 600 MET-minutes a week, which is 150 minutes of moderate activity at 4 METs or 75 minutes of vigorous activity at 8 METs. Averages and shares are shown to one decimal place, shares may not add to 100, and a report above four hours on an active day raises a check-the-entry warning rather than a refusal. Nothing is uploaded, stored or sent, and no weight, heart rate or device data is used.
